chapterNote: The harvest psalm — David's thanksgiving song that moves in three widening circles: the sanctuary, the world, and the fields. It begins in Zion, where praise waits in hushed readiness and vows are paid to the God who hears prayer — and to whom therefore all flesh will come. The atonement sits early and plainly: iniquities overpowered me, but our transgressions You Yourself cover over; blessed is the man You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts. Then the horizon widens to the God of creation — fixing mountains by His strength, quieting the roar of the seas and the tumult of the nations in the same breath, making the exits of dawn and dusk sing so that people at the ends of the earth stand in awe. And then the psalm gets its boots muddy: You visit the earth and drench it, the river of God is brimming, You prepare the grain, You soak the furrows and soften the ridges with showers and bless what sprouts; You crown the year with Your goodness and Your wagon-tracks drip with fatness — until the wilderness pastures overflow, the hills gird themselves with joy, the meadows wear flocks, the valleys wear grain, and the whole landscape shouts and sings. Every farmer's year, read as one long act of God.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David, a song. Praise waits for You in hushed stillness, O God, in Zion, and to You the vow will be paid in full.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] and Song [shir] of David. Praise [tehillah] waits ['is silent', dumiyyah, the KJV margin] for You, O God [Elohim], in Sion [Tsiyyon]: and unto You shall the vow [neder] be performed [shalam — paid, completed].
1.notes: dumiyyah (H1747), the stillness of Psalm 62:1: praise gathered in Tsiyyon and holding its breath before it breaks. The neder (H5088) shalam (H7999) is the thanksgiving vow being paid — this whole psalm may be the payment.

2.text: O Hearer of prayer, to You every mortal will make its way.
2.amp: O You that hear [shama] prayer [tephillah], unto You shall all flesh [basar] come [bo].
2.notes: God's defining title here is shomea tephillah (H8085, H8605), Hearer of prayer — and the logic is irresistible: where prayer is actually heard, kol basar (H1320), every mortal, will eventually make its way. The missionary horizon opens in the second verse (cf. Isaiah 66:23).

3.text: Iniquities have overpowered me — but our transgressions, You Yourself cover over and atone for them.
3.amp: Iniquities ['words, or, matters of iniquities', dibre avon, the KJV margin] prevail [gabar — overpower] against me: as for our transgressions [pesha], You shall purge them away [kaphar — cover, atone].
3.notes: The pilgrim arrives losing: dibre avonot (H5771), a whole docket of guilt, gabar (H1396) — stronger than he is. The turn is pronoun and verb: 'as for OUR pesha (H6588), YOU kaphar (H3722)' — the atonement-verb of the Day of Atonement, God covering what man could not overpower.

4.text: Oh the blessedness of the one You choose and bring near, to dwell in Your courts! We will be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, Your holy temple.
4.amp: Blessed [esher] is the man whom You choose [bachar], and cause to approach [qarav — bring near] unto You, that he may dwell [shakan] in Your courts [chatser]: we shall be satisfied [saba] with the goodness [tuv] of Your house [bayith], even of Your holy [qadosh] temple [hekal].
4.notes: The beatitude of election: bachar and qarav (H977, H7126) — chosen and brought near, both God's verbs, the worshiper the object of both. The result is saba (H7646) on the tuv (H2898) of His bayith: the satisfaction Psalm 63 promised in a desert, here at the source.

5.text: By awesome deeds in righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the confidence of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas;
5.amp: By terrible things [yare — awesome deeds] in righteousness [tsedek] will You answer [anah] us, O God [Elohim] of our salvation [yesha]; who art the confidence [mivtach] of all the ends [qatseh] of the earth [eretz], and of them that are afar off [rachoq] upon the sea [yam]:
5.notes: The second circle: God answers by norot (H3372), awe-deeds, done be-tsedek — and He is mivtach (H4009), the confidence, of everyone from the earth's qatseh to the far yam (H3220). Zion's God is the sailor's hope before the sailor knows His name.

6.text: who sets the mountains in place by His strength, girded with might;
6.amp: Which by His strength [koach] sets fast [kun — establishes] the mountains [har]; being girded [azar] with power [geburah]:
6.notes: kun (H3559), the establishing-verb, applied to the harim (H2022): the planet's most permanent things are His installations. azar geburah (H247, H1369), belted with might — creation as the work of a God dressed for labor.

7.text: who hushes the roar of the seas, the roar of their breakers, and the uproar of the nations.
7.amp: Which stills [shabach — quiets, hushes] the noise [shaon] of the seas [yam], the noise of their waves [gal], and the tumult [hamon] of the people [leom].
7.notes: shabach (H7623), elsewhere 'to praise', here in its sense of soothing to silence — the verb of Psalm 89:9. Two shaon (H7588) and then the hamon leummim: sea-roar and nation-roar in one sentence, both hushed by the same hand (cf. Psalm 46:6; Mark 4:39).

8.text: Those who dwell at the farthest ends stand in awe of Your signs; You make the gateways of morning and evening shout for joy.
8.amp: They also that dwell [yashab] in the uttermost parts [qatseh] are afraid [yare — awed] at Your tokens [ot — signs]: You make the outgoings [motsa] of the morning [boqer] and evening [erev] to rejoice ['sing', ranan, the KJV margin].
8.notes: The motsae boqer va-erev (H4161, H1242, H6153): the 'exits' of dawn and dusk — east and west, the places the sun comes out and goes in — made to ranan (H7442), ring with joy. Sunrise and sunset as the two daily choir entrances; the far-dwellers see the otot (H226) and go quiet.

9.text: You visit the earth and water it; You enrich it greatly with the river of God, which is full of water. You prepare their grain, for so You have prepared the earth.
9.amp: You visit [paqad — attend to, care for] the earth [eretz], and water [shuq] it: You greatly [rav] enrich [ashar] it with the river [peleg — the channel] of God [Elohim], which is full [male] of water [mayim]: You prepare [kun] them corn [dagan — grain], when You have so provided [kun] for it.
9.notes: The third circle, and the psalm's soil: paqad (H6485), the visiting-verb of divine care, applied to dirt. The peleg Elohim (H6388) is heaven's irrigation channel, male mayim, brim-full — and kun (H3559) twice: the grain (dagan, H1715) prepared because the ground was prepared first. Every harvest starts in God's planning.

10.text: You drench its furrows and settle its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless whatever springs up from it.
10.amp: You water [ravah — saturate] the ridges [telem — the furrows] thereof abundantly: You settle ['causest rain to descend into', nachath, the KJV margin] the furrows [gedud] thereof: You make it soft ['dissolvest it', mug, the KJV margin] with showers [rebibim]: You bless [barak] the springing [tsemach] thereof.
10.notes: Agronomy as doxology: ravah (H7301), soaked to saturation; mug (H4127), the clods dissolved by rebibim, the gentle showers; and barak (H1288) on the tsemach (H6780) — God's blessing spoken over green shoots. The same tsemach is the prophets' 'Branch' (cf. Zechariah 3:8); He blesses every sprout, and one Sprout above all.

11.text: You crown the year with Your goodness, and Your wagon tracks overflow with richness.
11.amp: You crown [atar] the year [shanah] with Your goodness ['of thy goodness', tov, the KJV margin]; and Your paths [magal — Your cart-tracks] drop [raaph — drip] fatness [deshen — richness].
11.notes: atar (H5849), the crowning-verb of Psalm 103:4, set on the shanah itself: the year wears goodness like a diadem. The magal (H4570) are wagon-ruts — God's harvest cart so overloaded that deshen (H1880), the rich fat of abundance, raaph (H7491), drips off it as it rolls.

12.text: They drip onto the pastures of the wilderness, and the hills gird themselves with rejoicing.
12.amp: They drop [raaph] upon the pastures [naah] of the wilderness [midbar]: and the little hills [gibah] rejoice ['are girded with joy', chagar gil, the KJV margin] on every side.
12.notes: The overflow reaches the neot midbar (H4057) — pasture the wilderness itself never planted — and the gebaot (H1389) chagar gil (H2296, H1524): the hills belt on rejoicing like a garment. Landscape dressed for a feast.

13.text: The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys wrap themselves in grain; they shout for joy — yes, they sing.
13.amp: The pastures [kar] are clothed [labash] with flocks [tson]; the valleys [emeq] also are covered over [ataph] with corn [bar — grain]: they shout for joy [rua], they also sing [shir].
13.notes: The wardrobe metaphor completes: labash (H3847) tson on the meadows, ataph bar (H1250) on the valleys — the land wearing its harvest. And the last verbs belong to the fields themselves: rua and shir (H7321, H7891), the war-shout and the song. Creation does not merely feed the choir; it joins it (cf. Psalm 96:12; Isaiah 55:12).
